text: Listen, heavens, and I will speak; hear, earth, the words of my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, my speech settle like dew, like fine rain on tender grass, like showers on the growing plants.

versions.text: Let my teaching fall like rain, my speech settle like dew, like showers on new grass, like raindrops on the green.
versions.explanation: "On the green" is an unnatural, elliptical noun phrase that reads awkwardly aloud and obscures the Hebrew parallel pair deshe' (fresh grass) / 'esev (plants, herbage). Making both objects explicit preserves the couplet's rhythm.

text: For I will proclaim the name of the LORD—ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock—his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness and without wrong, righteous and upright is he.
They have acted corruptly toward him; their blemish marks them as no children of his—a crooked and twisted generation.

versions.text: They have acted corruptly toward him; to their shame they are no longer his children—a crooked and twisted generation.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew mumam ("their blemish/defect") is dropped and replaced with the interpretive "to their shame." Retaining the idea of blemish keeps the sense of the difficult Hebrew line without adding a concept not in the text.

text: Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Is he not your Father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generations past. Ask your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will explain.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the human race, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD's portion is his people, Jacob his allotted inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in an empty, howling waste. He surrounded him and cared for him; he guarded him as the apple of his eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, that spreads its wings to catch them and carries them on its pinions,
the LORD alone led him; no foreign god was with him.
He set him astride the heights of the land and fed him the produce of the fields. He nourished him with honey from the rock, with oil from the flinty crag,
with curds from the herd and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs, with rams of Bashan and goats, with the finest of the wheat—and you drank the foaming blood of the grape.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked—you grew fat, thick, and sleek. He abandoned the God who made him and spurned the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange gods; with detestable things they provoked him to anger.
They sacrificed to demons, not to God—to gods they had never known, new gods, lately arrived, whom your fathers never feared.
You neglected the Rock who fathered you; you forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw it and rejected them, provoked to anger by his sons and daughters.
He said: I will hide my face from them and see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
They made me jealous with what is no god and angered me with their worthless idols. So I will make them jealous with what is no people; with a foolish nation I will provoke them.
For a fire has blazed up in my anger; it burns to the depths of Sheol. It devours the earth and its harvest and sets the foundations of the mountains ablaze.
I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend my arrows against them.
They will be wasted by hunger, consumed by burning fever and bitter plague. I will send against them the fangs of beasts, with the venom of things that glide in the dust.

versions.text: Wasted by hunger, consumed by burning fever and bitter plague—I will send against them the fangs of beasts and the venom of things that glide in the dust.
versions.explanation: As written, the opening participial phrases dangle with no subject in the sentence, which is confusing when read aloud. Supplying the subject makes the line clear while keeping the imagery intact.

text: In the street the sword will bereave, and in the rooms, terror—young man and young woman alike, nursing child and gray-haired elder.
I said I would blow them away, blot out their memory from mankind—
had I not feared the taunt of the enemy, that their adversaries would misunderstand and say, "Our own hand has triumphed; the LORD did none of this."

versions.text: had I not feared the taunt of the enemy, that their adversaries would misread it and say, "Our own hand has triumphed; the LORD did none of this."
versions.explanation: "Misread it" has no clear antecedent for "it" and sounds modern/idiomatic; "misunderstand" renders yenakkeru more naturally for oral reading.

text: For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise and would grasp this, and discern what their end would be.
How could one man chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock—even our enemies concede it.
Their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison; their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, the cruel poison of cobras.
Is this not stored up with me, sealed away in my treasuries?
Vengeance is mine, and repayment, for the time when their foot slips. Their day of disaster is near, and their doom rushes upon them.
For the LORD will vindicate his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees that their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free.
He will say: Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge—
the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise up and help you; let them be your shelter!
See now that I, I am he, and there is no god besides me. I put to death and I give life; I wound and I heal, and no one can deliver from my hand.
For I lift my hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will bring vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh—the blood of the slain and the captives, the heads of the enemy's leaders.
Rejoice, you nations, with his people! For he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will bring vengeance on his adversaries and make atonement for his land and his people.
Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you this day, so that you may command your children to be careful to do all the words of this law.
They are not empty words for you—they are your life. By them you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
That very same day the LORD said to Moses,
"Go up this mountain of the Abarim range, Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their possession.
There on the mountain you are about to climb, you will die and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.

versions.text: There on the mountain you climb, you will die and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
versions.explanation: The bare present "the mountain you climb" reads awkwardly aloud and blurs the sense of the Hebrew participle עֹלֶה, which points to the ascent Moses is about to make.

text: This is because both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin, and because you did not uphold my holiness among the Israelites.
You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it—the land I am giving to the Israelites.

versions.text: You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter the land I am giving to the Israelites."
versions.explanation: Repeating "the land" twice in one short sentence is heavy for oral reading; the revision keeps both Hebrew references while flowing more naturally.
